newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwanda denies claim its troops in Bukavu, Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda denies claim its troops in Bukavu, Zaire.

text.p: Rwanda's presidency on Thursday denied claims by aid workers in Geneva that Rwandan army commandos, in concert with ethnic Tutsi rebels, helped capture the eastern Zaire city of Bukavu.
"This is an outrageous story," Joseph Bideri, spokesman at the presidency, told Reuters by telephone from Kigali.
He said no Rwandan forces were inside Zaire where the Banyamulenge rebels are scoring military successes against government forces.
"The Rwandan troops did not capture Bukavu because we are not at war with Zaire. Zaire is at war with itself. If Bukavu will be captured it will be captured by Zaireans," Bideri said.
Western aid workers in Geneva said on Wednesday they had reports Rwandan commandos had entered Bukavu, just over the border from Rwanda, and had driven Zairean troops out.

Earlier on Wednesday the Rwandan military commander in the border town of Cyangugu, opposite Bukavu, said he sent "a good-sized" force of troops into Zaire after nightfall on Tuesday in retaliation for Zairean firing into Rwanda.
But he said the force withdrew a few hours later after pushing Zairean troops away from the border.
Bukavu's fate remained uncertain on Thursday. The Banyamulenge leader, Laurent Kabila, told Reuters his men controlled the city but there was no independent confirmation.
